title: Negative information questions with plural action verbs
summary: With plural persons, the negative verb is emme, ette or eivät. Miksi te ette tule? — Koska olemme sairaita.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with plural action verbs
prerequisiteSkills: Negative information questions with singular action verbs
objectives: Build a plural negative action question with the appropriate negative verb.
Keep the negative main verb unchanged when answering about a group.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The illative is an into/to form; mihin aikaan uses that form in a time expression.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.

With plural persons, the negative verb is emme, ette or eivät. The main verb's negative form does not take a plural personal ending: Miksi te ette tule? (“Why aren't you coming?” addressed to a group). The same negative stem serves every person.
keyPoints: Do not use etteko or ettekö in these ordinary information questions; use ette without a question suffix.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: A group addressed as te replies with emme plus the negative main-verb form: Emme juo kahvia (“We do not drink coffee”). With he, use eivät plus that same main-verb form. Keep the supplied partitive objects unchanged.
A natural short reply to “Miksi te ette tule?” is “Koska olemme sairaita.” (“Because we are ill.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: After emme or eivät, keep the negative main verb unchanged rather than adding -mme or -vat/-vät.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: olemme means we are here. Olla has the we-form olemme: ole- + -mme.
ovat means are here. Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.
emme means we do not here. Emme is the plural first-person negative verb.

juo means drink here. Juoda removes -da to form juo. This is the singular third-person affirmative form and, after a negative verb, the negative main-verb form; the long vowel does not lengthen further.
eivät means do not here. Eivät is the plural third-person negative verb.
syö means eat here. Syödä removes -dä to form syö, used as the singular third-person affirmative form or as the main verb after a negative verb.
tule means come here. Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.
mene means go here. Remove -n from menen to obtain negative mene, unchanged after every present negative verb.
lue means read here. Remove -n from luen to obtain negative lue. Keep the weak stem with k absent.
keyPoints: After emme or eivät, keep the negative main verb unchanged rather than adding -mme or -vat/-vät.

examples.english: We are not going to the library.

mene: go; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from menen to obtain negative mene, unchanged after every present negative verb.
